title: Migrating Layouts and Components
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and boundaries of Migrating Layouts and Components in the context of Pages Router and Legacy Application Maintenance.
Apply Moving shared UI into layouts in a minimal JavaScript/JSX or configuration example and describe its expected result.
Verify the example with one relevant edge or failure case and identify version/runtime assumptions.

content.intro: This lesson develops Migrating Layouts and Components in the supplied Next.js curriculum. The list below preserves its named syllabus subtopics and ties them to a small example you can inspect and adapt.
content.why_it_matters: The Pages Router remains relevant for maintenance. Keep its conventions distinct from the App Router and migrate incrementally with regression tests. In practice, moving shared UI into layouts should be understood well enough to explain the expected behavior and how it can fail.

content_blocks.run_instructions: This is an inspectable example, not an arbitrary-code runner inside CodeLeaf. Start from a separate JavaScript App Router project created with `npx create-next-app@latest my-next-app --js --app`, put the snippet in the named or relevant file, and run `npm run dev`. Examples that call application-owned helpers, databases, authentication, or third-party APIs require those dependencies and appropriate environment variables. Use `npm run build` to validate a production build after adapting it.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original snippet, reset the example data and request state, then rerun the same normal case and one empty, invalid, slow, denied, or failed case as relevant. Remove any test records and use non-production credentials.

content_blocks.text: This JavaScript-first course uses the Next.js 16 documentation snapshot checked on 2026-10-18. Legacy note: this lesson is for existing applications and migration. New application examples should prefer the App Router unless a project requirement says otherwise. TypeScript is an optional parallel skill, not a requirement for these examples. Confirm any experimental or configuration-dependent API in the exact version installed in your learning project.

content.task: Create or inspect a minimal example for “Migrating Layouts and Components”. Include the syllabus concept “Moving shared UI into layouts”, state its expected output, and verify one normal and one boundary or failure case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named concept rather than only mentioning it.
Expected output and the project/runtime needed to reproduce it are documented.
At least one boundary, empty, loading, denied, or failure case is tested or explicitly reasoned about.
Secrets and trusted server operations stay on the server; UI behavior remains semantic and accessible where relevant.
hints: Start with the smallest observable part of “Moving shared UI into layouts”.
Predict the output, change one input at a time, and compare the result with your expectation.
If results differ, check the route/file convention, current Next.js and Node.js versions, server logs, and whether the behavior is cache-dependent.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a development preview as proof that the production application is correct.
common_mistakes.why: Caching, environment configuration, deployment constraints, and error handling can differ between development and production.
common_mistakes.fix: Run the relevant targeted tests and a production build, then verify the deployed/runtime-specific behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Relying on client-only checks for sensitive data or mutations.
common_mistakes.why: Requests can be sent without using the visible UI.
common_mistakes.fix: Authenticate, authorize, validate inputs, and check resource ownership inside the trusted server operation.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a Next.js behavior is universal across releases.
common_mistakes.why: Rendering, caching, config, and request processing APIs evolve between versions.
common_mistakes.fix: Name the target release and check its matching official docs before publishing or upgrading the example.
